brief.headline: Ask for ₹32.69 L/yr saved by matching your best laminate price, and offer 15-day faster payment in exchange for another cut — they need cash faster than most (stuck 81 days vs 46).

priceAsk.summary: Match the ₹290.00/KG your cheapest supplier charges for similar laminates
priceAsk.target: ₹32.69 L/yr saving by closing the gap to ₹290.00/KG (from ₹294.03–308.30/KG on top SKUs)
priceAsk.basis: Market research shows pharma ORS sachet laminates ask ₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg — their ₹294–308 is top of fair band. Shrinath Roto Pack Pvt Ltd already gives you ₹290.00/KG for the same items, so hold GEEP to that. They're charging 1.4% to 6.3% more for no reason.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 Days After Receipt to 15 Days After Receipt in exchange for a further price cut of about 4%
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹1.16 Cr cash freed up for us if we shave 15 days off the 30-day term

brief.financialLeverage: They're middling health — CRISIL BB+ / Stable, but they stopped sharing info with the rater, so treat that rating as stale. They keep only 1.1% profit on every ₹100 they sell, much thinner than similar firms (2.1%), so a huge price squeeze could hurt supply. But their cash is stuck for 81 days, well longer than the 46 days typical at peer firms — so they really want faster payment. You're 9.72% of their ₹291.36 Cr sales, so you're a big customer they can't afford to lose. Push hard on terms and on closing the ₹32.69 L price gap, but don't squeeze so tight you break them.

evidence.point: Their cash is stuck for 81 days, much longer than similar firms
You're nearly a tenth of their business
They keep very thin profit — only 1.1% of sales
You're paying ₹32.69 L/yr more than the best price you already get
evidence.figure: ₹32.69 L annual excess vs ₹290.00/KG from Shrinath Roto Pack Pvt Ltd

evidence.point: Market asks for pharma ORS laminates run ₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg — their prices sit at the top of fair
evidence.figure: ₹205–305/kg band, ₹250/kg typical; verdict MARKET-FAIR (top of fair band)

evidence.point: Rating agency stopped getting their data — the BB+ / Stable may be out of date

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter, already supplies FDC a bit, health C (59/100), ₹2758.00 Cr revenue — proven and scalable for laminate sachets

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant doing both film substrate and conversion, health C (46/100), ₹16492.00 Cr revenue — can handle GEEP volumes easily

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of global Constantia group, does pharma blister and sachet laminates, health D (31/100), ₹222.04 Cr revenue — strong fit for ORS sachets

risks: They're 76% of your Laminates spend (₹28.31 Cr) — you have almost no backup right now, so line up and qualify a second source (Huhtamaki or UFLEX) before you push them too hard.
CRISIL BB+ but the company won't share data with the rater — treat their financial health as a question mark and keep supply continuity top of mind.
GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, and pending legal cases on record — watch for any hiccup in deliveries or quality if they're distracted by compliance trouble.
Their profit is only 1.1% — if you cut price by more than a couple of percent without giving them faster payment in return, you risk squeezing them into losses and jeopardizing supply.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹32.69 L a year more than our best laminate price — let's talk about closing that gap and moving you to faster payment so we both win.
